small-behavior.overview: Adds a gh uptime command that reads GitHub Status without GitHub API authentication, evaluates either the whole service or one component, and reports or waits on that state for humans and scripts.

intent.statement: Let an Operator or automation observe GitHub service availability even while the authenticated GitHub API is degraded.

outcomes.text: Fetch public service status without sending the gh authentication token.
Render whole-platform or component status for humans and JSON consumers.
Let automation fail on degradation or wait until recovery.

nodes.label: Expose gh uptime
nodes.description: The root CLI makes the new standalone command available.

nodes.label: Resolve requested status view
nodes.description: Flags select all services or one component, JSON output, exit behavior, and optional polling.

nodes.label: Fetch public status summary
nodes.description: A plain timed HTTP client reads the public Statuspage summary endpoint without gh auth injection.

nodes.label: Evaluate target availability
nodes.description: The command filters non-service rows, finds the requested component, and derives an operational boolean.

nodes.label: Wait while target is degraded
nodes.description: Watch mode sleeps and retries until the selected target becomes operational.

nodes.label: Report status to human or automation
nodes.description: The result is rendered, exported as JSON, and optionally converted into a non-zero exit.

claims.statement: Watch mode never rejects an unknown component.
claims.condition: The Operator combines --watch with a component name absent from the Statuspage response.
claims.consequence: The command treats the target as perpetually non-operational and polls until interrupted instead of reporting the invalid name.
limitations: Static inspection does not observe a live Statuspage response changing its component set.

limitations: Test source is not evidence that those tests executed for this exact head.

excluded: No full base/head checkout was available.
No provider check run proves the tests executed on this exact head.

limitations: The public endpoint's live behavior and rate limits were not exercised.
Repository context is limited to patches and shallow root metadata.

intent.statement: Make GitHub incident state consumable by people and scripts without depending on api.github.com.

outcomes.text: Reach Statuspage independently of gh authentication.

nodes.description: The root command resolves component, watch, interval, exit-code, and exporter choices.

large-cross-cutting.overview: Extends api_host routing across many remaining gh commands by adding a flexible shared request surface, mapping configured API hosts back to credentials, migrating direct HTTP call sites, and exercising the result through a blackhole gateway harness.

intent.statement: Route nearly all CLI API traffic through each host's configured api_host without losing request-specific behavior or credential selection.

outcomes.text: Resolve api_host in both host-to-endpoint and endpoint-to-host directions.
Preserve streaming, headers, redirects, scopes, and response access behind a shared API client surface.
Move remaining direct request call sites onto host-aware request paths.
Make routing bypasses observable with a gateway and acceptance subset.

nodes.label: Resolve configured API host
nodes.description: Authentication config maps a canonical host to api_host and can reverse that mapping for later credential lookup.

nodes.label: Attach canonical-host credential
nodes.description: When the request target has no direct token, the auth transport reverse-resolves api_host and uses the associated host token.

nodes.label: Build request with preserved semantics
nodes.description: The shared client exposes response-returning, context-aware, redirect-sensitive, header, and endpoint-scope options.

nodes.label: Route relative API request to api_host
nodes.description: Command request construction substitutes api_host for REST and GraphQL relative requests while leaving absolute URLs unchanged.

nodes.label: Send command traffic through shared client
nodes.description: Gist, release, repository, run, search, extension, auth, and other call sites stop bypassing the host-aware request surface.

nodes.label: Observe requests at gateway
nodes.description: A TLS reverse proxy records method, path, target host, auth presence, and outcome while rewriting upstream host references.

nodes.label: Fail acceptance on routing bypass
nodes.description: The harness blackholes github.com and runs selected acceptance paths through the gateway; provider checks report builds and integration suites passed.

claims.statement: A shared api_host can select the wrong canonical-host credential.
claims.condition: Two configured hosts point to the same api_host and a request reaches that API host without a directly configured token.
claims.consequence: Reverse lookup chooses the first host in Hosts order, so the transport can attach that host's token to traffic intended for the other host.
limitations: The fixture does not establish whether sharing one api_host is supported or prevented elsewhere.
No runtime fixture exercises two canonical hosts behind one gateway.

claims.statement: A review comment identifies a mismatch between swapURLHost documentation and implementation, but no adverse behavior is established.
limitations: Whether replacing the original port is intended is not resolved by this snapshot.
